Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 1–6:

Explanation of the words:

Al-hamd lillah (all praise is due to Allah): al-hamd is the ascribing of beauty (of attributes), and Allah is a proper name (ʿalam) for the Essence of the Lord, exalted is He.

Al-Kitab (the Book): the Noble Qur'an.

Wa lam yaj'al lahu ʿiwajan (and has not made in it any crookedness): i.e., no deviation from the truth and no lack of moderation in its wording or its meanings.

Qayyiman (upright): i.e., moderate, with neither excess nor deficiency in all that it contains and calls to, of tawhid, worship, manners, laws and rulings.

Basan shadidan (severe punishment): punishment of great severity and harshness, a terrible torment in the Hereafter.

Min ladunhu (from Him): from Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Ajran hasanan (a goodly reward): i.e., Paradise, for it is the reward of the believers who do righteous deeds.

Kabura kalimah (a grave word has come out): i.e., their fabrication is great, namely their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah.

In yaqulun illa kadhiban (they say nothing but a lie): i.e., they say nothing but a sheer lie that has no reality outside.

Bakhi'un nafsaka (you would be killing yourself): killing yourself, like one who commits suicide.

Bihadha al-hadith asafan (over this discourse, out of grief): i.e., over the Qur'an, out of the sorrow that is intense grief.

Explanation of the verses:

In the opening of Surah al-Kahf, Allah, exalted is He, informs that He alone deserves praise, and that all praise is due to Allah, mentioning what necessitates it: that He sent down upon His servant and Messenger Muhammad ﷺ the magnificent Book, which is the great, noble Qur'an. He says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down upon His servant the Book﴾. And His saying, ﴿and has not made in it any crookedness﴾, i.e., He has not made in that great Book any crookedness, that is, any deviation from the truth and any lack of moderation in its wording and meanings. It is a straight speech which secures for whoever holds to it every happiness and perfection in both lives. And His saying ﴿upright﴾, i.e., moderate, free from excess and deficiency, an upright guardian over the earlier scriptures, prevailing over them: what is true in them is affirmed and what is false is refuted.

And His saying ﴿that He may warn with severe punishment from Him﴾, i.e., He sent down the Book, free from crookedness and upright, so that it may warn the wrongdoers among the people of polytheism and sins of a severe punishment, in this world and the Hereafter, which will descend upon them from their Lord, those who disbelieved in Him, associated others with Him, disobeyed Him, and denied His Messenger and disobeyed him. And so that, through it, it may also give good news to ﴿the believers who do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., it informs them of what gladdens them and delights their hearts: that for them, with their Lord, are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and warn﴾ specifically refers to those who fabricate against Allah and slander Him by attributing a son to Him, saying: ﴿Allah has taken a son﴾. They are the Jews and the Christians and some of the polytheists of the Arabs who said that the angels are the daughters of Allah! This is what His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿and warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾. It is a saying they inherited, of which none of them has any knowledge; it is merely a lie that they pass along among themselves. Therefore Allah has condemned this saying of theirs, and the intelligent have marvelled at it. So He says: ﴿A grave word it is that comes out of their mouths﴾, i.e., their saying "Allah has taken a son" is great, a word they utter which comes out of their mouths and nothing more, for it has no reality at all. He then affirms the denunciation of them, saying: ﴿They speak nothing but a lie﴾, i.e., they say nothing but a sheer lie that rests on no foundation of truth whatsoever.

And His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps, if they do not believe in this discourse﴾ admonishes His Messenger and lightens for him what he finds within himself of sorrow over his people's failure to believe, their persistence in disbelief and denial, and what they demand of him of signs. That is: perhaps, O Our Messenger, you would be killing yourself following your people's refusal to believe in you, in your Book and in the guidance you brought, out of grief for them and distress at them. So do not do so, but be patient with the decree of your Lord, for He will surely fulfil His promise to you of victory over your denying people.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to praise Allah for His bounties and His great favours.

2- Only one who possesses what necessitates praise is to be praised; otherwise the praise is a lie and falsehood.

3- The great status of the Noble Qur'an and its freedom from excess, deficiency and deviation in all that it brings.

4- Explanation of the mission of the Qur'an, which is to give good news to the people of faith and to warn the people of polytheism and disbelief.

5- Condemnation of lying against Allah and attributing to Him what is unworthy of His majesty and perfection, such as offspring and the like.

6- Prohibition of suicide and of killing oneself out of grief, fear, or the like, or out of anger or deprivation.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and warn﴾ specifically refers to those who fabricate against Allah and slander Him by attributing a son to Him, saying: ﴿Allah has taken a son﴾. They are the Jews and the Christians and some of the polytheists of the Arabs who said that the angels are the daughters of Allah! This is what His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿and warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾. It is a saying they inherited, of which none of them has any knowledge; it is merely a lie that they pass along among themselves. Therefore Allah has condemned this saying of theirs, and the intelligent have marvelled at it. So He says: ﴿A grave word it is that comes out of their mouths﴾, i.e., their saying "Allah has taken a son" is great, a word they utter which comes out of their mouths and nothing more, for it has no reality at all. He then affirms the denunciation of them, saying: ﴿They speak nothing but a lie﴾, i.e., they say nothing but a sheer lie that rests on no foundation of truth whatsoever.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to praise Allah for His bounties and His great favours.

2- Only one who possesses what necessitates praise is to be praised; otherwise the praise is a lie and falsehood.

3- The great status of the Noble Qur'an and its freedom from excess, deficiency and deviation in all that it brings.

4- Explanation of the mission of the Qur'an, which is to give good news to the people of faith and to warn the people of polytheism and disbelief.

5- Condemnation of lying against Allah and attributing to Him what is unworthy of His majesty and perfection, such as offspring and the like.

6- Prohibition of suicide and of killing oneself out of grief, fear, or the like, or out of anger or deprivation.

Ar-Raqīm: a stone tablet on which the names of the People of the Cave were inscribed.

Āwā al-fityatu ilā al-kahf: they took it as a shelter and a dwelling in which they settled.

Al-fityah: the plural of fatā, meaning believing young men.

Hayyi' lanā min amrinā rashadan: that is, make easy for us a path of right guidance and direction.

Fa-ḍarabnā ʿalā ādhānihim: that is, We placed a veil over their ears that prevents them from hearing sounds and movements.

Sinīna ʿadadan: that is, a number of years.

Thumma baʿathnāhum: that is, roused them from their sleep, meaning We woke them up.

Amadan: that is, a known, defined period.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have made that which is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾, of animals, trees, plants, rivers and seas. And His saying ﴿that We may test them﴾, that is, to test them, ﴿as to which of them is best in deed﴾, that is, which of them is most detached from it, most compliant with Our command and prohibition, and most active in it through obedience to Us. And His saying: ﴿And indeed, We will make that which is upon it into barren dust﴾, that is, indeed We will ruin it on a day among the days, after its cultivation, its freshness and its adornment, making it ﴿barren dust﴾, that is, dust with no vegetation in it. Therefore, do not grieve, O Our Messenger, and do not be distressed by what you encounter from your people, for the end of this life, for whose sake they have opposed you and disobeyed Us, is that it becomes barren dust.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs as a wonder?﴾ That is, did you suppose, O Prophet, that the People of the Cave, that is the grotto in the cave, and the Raqīm, which is the tablet on which were inscribed the names of the People of the Cave, their lineages and their story, were a greater wonder among Our signs? ﴿were among Our signs as a wonder﴾, that is, they were more wondrous than Our signs in creation and creatures, the heavens and the earth; rather, among the creatures of God there is what is far more wondrous.

His saying: ﴿When the youths sought refuge in the cave﴾. This begins the mention of their wondrous story, that is, mention to those who ask you about the story of these youths, when they sought refuge in the grotto in the cave and settled there, taking it as a shelter and a dwelling, fleeing from their disbelieving people lest they tempt them away from their religion. They were seven young men, with a dog of theirs, and they said, asking their Lord: ﴿Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and make easy for us from our affair a right course﴾, that is, give us mercy from Your presence that accompanies us in this emigration from polytheism and the polytheists, ﴿and make easy for us from our affair a right course﴾, that is, and facilitate for us in our affair, in our flight from the lands of the polytheists out of fear for our religion, ﴿a right course﴾, that is, rectitude, goodness and deliverance from the people of disbelief and falsehood.

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī said in his tafsir of these verses: The scholars have differed concerning the reason these youths went to the cave that God mentioned in His Book. Some of them said: the reason was that they were Muslims upon the religion of ʿĪsā, and there was a worshipping king who worshipped idols who invited them to worship idols, so they fled with their religion from him, fearing that he would tempt them away from their religion or kill them, and they hid in the cave.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We placed a veil over their ears in the cave for a number of years﴾, that is, We placed over their ears a veil preventing them from hearing sounds and movements, so they slept in their cave for a number of counted years, namely three hundred and nine years. They turned from side to side by the gentle care and management of God for them, until He roused them from their sleep. This was God's response to them when they called upon Him saying: ﴿Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself﴾. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We roused them﴾, that is, from their sleep and slumber, ﴿that We might know which of the two parties was most precise in computing the duration they remained﴾, that is, in the cave, ﴿a term﴾. That is, so that We may know with knowledge of witnessing, and so that My servants may look and know which of the two groups that disagreed about the length of their stay in the cave was more precise regarding the period of their stay in the cave, since the people differed into two parties: one party says they remained in their cave so many years, and another says they remained until such-and-such a limit of years.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the reason for the presence of adornment on this earth: it is a trial and a test for people, so that the one who renounces it, who knows its triviality and the speed of its passing, becomes manifest, and so that the one who desires it and grovels after it, who disobeys God for its sake, becomes manifest.

2- Affirmation of the annihilation of everything on the earth, until it remains barren dust and a smooth plain in which no crookedness or elevation is seen.

3- Affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ by answering those who asked about the People of the Cave, with brevity and with detail.

4- Affirmation of monotheism within the story of the People of the Cave, for they fled with their religion out of fear of polytheism and disbelief.

5- God's response to the supplication of His believing, monotheist servants: He responded to the youths, sheltered them in the cave and protected them until He roused them after the change of conditions and the transformation of the people and the lands.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verse 13–16:

Explanation of the words:

*Nabba'hum bil-haqq* (نبأهم بالحق): that is, He informs them of their wondrous account with truth and certainty.

*Wa zadnahum huda* (وزادهم هدى): that is, faith and insight in their religion and knowledge of their Lord, to the point that they were patient in emigrating.

*Wa rabatna 'ala qulubihim* (وربطنا على قلوبهم): that is, We strengthened them so that their resolve grew firm, until they spoke the word of truth before an unjust ruler.

*Lan nad'u min dunihi ilaha* (لن ندعوا من دونه إلها): we will not worship any other god besides Him.

*Lawla ya'tuna 'alayhim bi-sultan* (لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان): that is, why do they not bring a strong proof establishing the validity of their worship?

*'Ala Allahi kadhiba* (على الله كذبا): that is, by taking gods besides Him, the Exalted, whom they call upon and worship.

*Fa'wu ila al-kahf* (فأووا إلى الكهف): that is, go down into the cave and conceal yourselves in it from the eyes of your enemies, the polytheists.

*Yanshur lakum rabbukum min rahmatihi* (ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته): that is, He will spread out His mercy upon you by saving you from what you fled from.

*Wa yuhayyi' lakum min amrikum* (ويهيئ لكم من أمركم): and He will facilitate for you your affair in which you are in distress and sorrow.

*Mirfaqa* (مرفقا): that is, that by which you are provided and benefit, such as food, drink and shelter.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, the Exalted, had mentioned a summary of the story of the People of the Cave, He began to detail it: ﴿We relate to you their story with truth﴾, that is, We, the Lord of might and majesty, relate to you, O Messenger, the account of the People of the Cave with the established truth about which there is no doubt. ﴿They were youths﴾, plural of fata, ﴿who believed in their Lord﴾, that is, they affirmed His existence, the obligation of worshipping Him and of professing His Oneness in worship. And His saying ﴿and We increased them in guidance﴾, that is, guidance to knowing the truth of what is loved by Allah and what is hated by Him.

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We fortified their hearts﴾, that is, We strengthened their resolve by firming up their hearts, so that they stood up and said before the chiefs and in the presence of a disbelieving king: ﴿Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, we have no lord other than Him. We will not call upon any god besides Him, whatever his station, for if we acknowledged the worship of another, we would have uttered an extravagant word, which is falsehood and exaggeration concerning Him. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿These, our people, have taken gods besides Him﴾ informs of the speech of the youths when Allah fortified their hearts, as they stood against the wicked polytheists and said: ﴿These, our people, have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring a clear authority concerning them?﴾, that is, why do they not bring a clear proof establishing the worship of these idols besides Allah? And from where would that come, when there is no god but Allah?!

And His saying: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah a lie?﴾ Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, negates that there could be anyone more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah by taking gods to worship alongside Him, under the pretext of seeking intercession through them and the slogan of drawing near to Allah through their means!! And His saying, concerning the words of the People of the Cave to one another: ﴿And when you have removed yourselves from them and what they worship other than Allah﴾, that is, the idols and images, ﴿then take refuge in the cave﴾, that is, betake yourselves to the cave called "Najlus" ﴿your Lord will spread for you of His mercy﴾, that is, He will extend to you of His mercy by facilitating for you the way out of the affair in which you have been thrown by the disbelieving king "Decius" ﴿and will prepare for you of your affair facility﴾, that is, that by which you are provided, such as food, drink and security in your new refuge to which you have retreated, fleeing with your religion and hiding from your pursuer who seeks you to tempt you in your religion or to kill you.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood through the mention of the story of the People of the Cave.

2- Affirmation that faith increases and decreases.

3- The virtue of boldness in truth and declaring it, even if it leads to killing, beating or imprisonment.

4- Affirmation of monotheism, that there is no god but Allah, on the tongue of the People of the Cave.

5- The invalidity of worshipping other than Allah, for there is no rational or transmitted evidence for it.

6- Shirk is injustice and falsehood, and the polytheist is unjust, a fabricator and a liar.

7- Affirmation of the obligation of emigration in the way of Allah.

8- The virtue of seeking refuge in Allah, the Exalted, and asking His protection for His servant, and that Allah suffices whoever sincerely takes refuge in Him.

1- Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood through the mention of the story of the People of the Cave.

2- Affirmation that faith increases and decreases.

3- The virtue of boldness in truth and declaring it, even if it leads to killing, beating or imprisonment.

4- Affirmation of monotheism, that there is no god but Allah, on the tongue of the People of the Cave.

5- The invalidity of worshipping other than Allah, for there is no rational or transmitted evidence for it.

6- Shirk is injustice and falsehood, and the polytheist is unjust, a fabricator and a liar.

7- Affirmation of the obligation of emigration in the way of Allah.

8- The virtue of seeking refuge in Allah, the Exalted, and asking His protection for His servant, and that Allah suffices whoever sincerely takes refuge in Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 17–18:

Explanation of the words:

Tazawaru: i.e., they incline.

Taqriduhum: they leave them and pass by them, so that they are not struck (by the sun).

Fi fajwatin minhu: a spacious part of the cave, where they receive the coolness of the wind and its breeze.

Min ayati Allah: i.e., signs of His power.

Ayqadan: plural of yaqizh, meaning alert, because their eyes are open.

Bil-wasid: the courtyard of the cave.

Ru'ban: God, by means of it, prevented (people) from entering upon them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to present the story of the People of the Cave. The Exalted says, addressing His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And you would see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave﴾, i.e., it turns away from it to the right, ﴿and when it sets, passing them by on the left﴾, i.e., it leaves them and passes by them so that they are not struck by it on the left side. His saying: ﴿while they are in a spacious part of it﴾, i.e., a spacious part of the cave where they receive the coolness of the wind and its breeze. His saying: ﴿That is among the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., that mentioned inclination of the sun away from them when it rises and its passing them by when it sets is among the proofs of the power of Allah the Exalted, and of His mercy toward His friends and His kindness to them. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whomever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, but whomever He sends astray, you will not find for him a guardian to guide him﴾ informs that guidance is in His hand, and likewise misguidance, so the servant should ask his Lord for guidance to His straight path, and seek refuge in Him from manifest error, for whomever Allah misguides, there will be found for him no guardian who guides him under any circumstances. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you would think them awake, while they are asleep﴾, i.e., when you look at them you suppose them awake, meaning alert, because their eyes are open, while they are asleep, sleeping, not sensing anyone and not aware. His saying: ﴿And their dog, stretching out its forelegs at the threshold﴾, i.e., their dog that went out with them, which was a hunting dog, ﴿stretching out its forelegs at the threshold﴾, i.e., at the courtyard of the cave. 3- Demonstration of the wondrous arrangement of Allah the Exalted and His disposal of His creatures. Glory be to Him, the great, all-knowing, all-wise God.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 19–21:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Thus We awakened them﴾: That is, just as We caused them to sleep that long, extraordinary sleep, We also raised them from their slumber in an extraordinary awakening. So there was a sign in their sleeping and a sign in their waking.

﴿How long have you remained?﴾: That is, in the cave, asleep.

﴿A day or part of a day﴾: Because they had entered the cave in the morning and awoke in the evening.

﴿With this silver of yours﴾: With the silver coins that you have.

﴿To the city﴾: That is, the city that was called Ephesus, which is Tarsus today.

﴿Which is purest in food﴾: That is, which of the city's foods is most lawful, meaning the most permissible.

﴿And let him be discreet﴾: That is, let him go to buy the food and return gently and discreetly.

﴿They would stone you﴾: That is, they would kill you by pelting you with stones.

﴿We caused them to be found﴾: We let the people of their town become aware of them.

﴿That they might know﴾: That is, their people, that the Resurrection is true, for both bodies and spirits together.

﴿When they disputed among themselves﴾: That is, the disbelievers said, "Build over them," meaning build a structure around them that would shelter them.

﴿So they said﴾: That is, the believers and the disbelievers, regarding the matter of building over them.

﴿Those who prevailed in their affair said﴾: They are the believers: "We will surely take over them a place of worship in which to pray."

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of the People of the Cave. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Thus We awakened them so that they might question one another﴾: that is, just as We made them sleep for three hundred and nine years, preserving their bodies and garments from decay and preventing anyone from reaching them, this is among the manifestations of Our power and great dominion. We raised them from their long sleep so that they might question one another. One of them asked, inquiring, "How long have you remained?" Some of them answered, "We have remained a day or part of a day," because they had retreated to the cave in the morning and were raised from their slumber in the evening. Another answered with a reply pleasing to all, which is His saying, ﴿Your Lord knows best how long you have remained﴾, so they entrusted the matter to Him. They were hungry, so they said to one of them, ﴿Send one of you with this silver of yours﴾, pointing to a silver coin they had with them, ﴿to the city﴾, which is Ephesus, from which they had fled with their religion. His saying, ﴿Let him see which is purest in food, and bring you provision from it﴾: that is, let the one you send to buy food see which kinds of food are purest, meaning cleanest from the unlawful and from what is repugnant. ﴿And bring you provision from it﴾ to eat, to satisfy your hunger. ﴿And let him be discreet in his purchase, going and returning, so that no one becomes aware of you.﴾ He gave a reason for this saying with His words, ﴿For if they gain power over you﴾, that is, they discover you, ﴿they will stone you﴾, that is, kill you by pelting you with stones, ﴿or return you to their religion﴾, the religion of polytheism, by compulsion and force. ﴿And you would never succeed then, ever.﴾ That is, you would never succeed in being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise if you returned to disbelief and polytheism, disbelieving and associating partners with your Lord.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And thus We caused them to be found﴾: that is, just as We made them sleep that long period and raised them so that they might question one another, so that they would increase in faith and knowledge of God's guardianship and His protection of His friends, ﴿We caused them to be found﴾ by the people of their city, who had divided into two groups: one group believed that resurrection is true and that it is of bodies and spirits, and another group said that the resurrection is only of spirits, not bodies, as is the belief of the Christians to this day. God put the youths to sleep, raised them, and caused these disputing people to find them, so it became clear to them that God is able to resurrect people alive, in bodies and spirits, as He raised the People of the Cave. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And thus We caused them to be found, that they might know﴾: that is, those who disputed about the matter of resurrection, that the promise of God is true, which is what He promised people: that He will raise them after their death on the Day of Resurrection to call them to account and recompense them for their deeds.

﴿And that the Hour is not in doubt about it﴾. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿When they disputed among themselves over their affair﴾: that is, We caused them to be found at a time when the people of the town were disputing about the matter of resurrection and the life to come, whether it is of bodies and spirits or of spirits without bodies. Through this event it became clear to them that resurrection is true and that it is of bodies and spirits together. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So they said: Build over them a structure﴾, and leave them in the cave, that is, seal the entrance of the cave over them and leave them within it, because after they found them, they died. ﴿Their Lord knows best about them﴾ and about their condition.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Those who prevailed in their affair said: We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾: that is, those who prevailed over the matter of the youths said, since the ruler was Muslim among them, ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾, that is, for prayer in it. And indeed they built a place of worship close to the mouth of the cave.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Manifestations of God's power, knowledge, and wisdom.

2- The obligation to seek lawful food, drink, and other things.

3- Dying in polytheism and disbelief prevents success on the Day of Resurrection forever.

4- Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense, which the people of Makkah deny.

5- Confirmation of the saying of the Messenger ﷺ, "May Allah curse the Jews and Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship," and his saying, "When there was among them a righteous man and he died, they built a place of worship over his grave and made in it those images; those are the worst of creation on the Day of Resurrection" (in the two Sahihs).

6- Confirmation of the saying of the Messenger ﷺ, "You will surely follow the ways of those before you, span by span and cubit by cubit," for the Muslims have built mosques over the graves of the friends of God and the righteous after the preferred generations, until it has become rare to find an old mosque free of a grave or graves.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 18, Verses 22–26**

**Explanation of the words:**

**رجماً بالغيب (rajman bil-ghayb):** That is, a casting of conjecture without certain knowledge.

**ولا يشرك في حكمه أحداً (wa-la yushriku fi hukmihi ahadan):** Because He is free of need of anything other than Himself, and has no partner.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The discussion continues concerning the People of the Cave. Allah, exalted is He, informs that those who dispute about the matter of the People of the Cave will say, some of them, that they were three, the fourth being their dog, and others will say they were five, the sixth being their dog. **﴿Rajman bil-ghayb﴾** means a casting of the unseen without certain knowledge. Others will say they were seven, the eighth being their dog. Then Allah commanded His Messenger to say to his companions regarding those statements: **﴿My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few﴾**, meaning that none among the people knows their number except a few. Ibn 'Abbas said, "I am among that few, and their number is seven, the eighth being their dog." Perhaps he understood this from the context of the verse, since Allah mentioned that the first and second groups spoke by way of *rajm bil-ghayb* and not by way of knowledge and certainty, and He remained silent about the third group. This indicates that they were seven, the eighth being their dog, and Allah knows best.

As for His saying, **﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an apparent argument﴾**, that means: do not dispute with the People of the Book regarding the matter of the People of the Cave except with a clear and gentle argument, by mentioning what We have related to you, without denying them and without agreeing with them.

As for His saying, **﴿And do not consult any of them concerning them﴾**, that means: concerning the People of the Cave, **﴿from among them﴾**, that is, from among the People of the Book, **﴿any one﴾**. This is because they do not know their number; they speak only by guesswork and conjecture, not by knowledge and certainty.

As for His saying, **﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," without [adding], "If Allah wills"﴾**: that means, O Muhammad, do not say about something you intend to do in the future, "I will do such and such," unless you say, "If Allah wills." This is because when the delegation of Quraysh, at the instigation of the Jews, asked him about three matters—the soul, the People of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn—he (ﷺ) said to those who asked, "I will answer you tomorrow," awaiting revelation, and did not say, "If Allah wills." So his Lord disciplined him by withholding revelation from him for half a month, and He sent down this surah, which contains this discipline for him (ﷺ).

As for His saying, **﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾**, that means: when you forget the exception that We taught you, then mention it, even after some time, so that you may be free from distress.

As for expiation (*kaffara*), it is obligatory [in cases where the exception was not made], unless the exception is connected to the speech itself.

As for His saying, **﴿And say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance"﴾**, that means: and say, after forgetting and the required exception, **﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right guidance﴾**, that is, perhaps Allah, exalted is He, will guide me and set me on the most upright course, to something more evident as a proof of my prophethood than what you asked me about as a test for me.

As for His saying, **﴿And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and exceeded by nine﴾**, Allah, exalted is He, informs that the youths remained in their cave in sleep from the hour they entered it until Allah caused their people to discover them: three hundred years by the solar reckoning, plus an addition of nine years by the lunar reckoning.

As for His saying, **﴿Say, "Allah is most knowing of how long they remained"﴾**: with this He refuted those among the People of the Book who said that the three hundred and nine years were counted from the hour they entered the cave until the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). Allah nullified this first by affirming the three hundred and nine, second by His saying, **﴿Allah is most knowing of how long they remained﴾**, third by His saying, **﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾**, that is, what is hidden in them, fourth by His saying, **﴿How clearly He sees and how clearly He hears﴾**, that is, how clearly He sees His creation and how clearly He hears their statements, since nothing of their affairs and conditions is hidden from Him, and fifth by His saying, **﴿For them, other than Him, there is no protector﴾**, that is, for the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, besides Him, exalted is He, **﴿no guardian﴾**, that is, no helper, **﴿and He does not share His authority with anyone﴾**, because of His independence from all else and because He has no partner in any way at all.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. Clarification of the disagreement among the People of the Book and their failure to establish historical events accurately.
2. Clarification of the number of the youths of the Cave, and that they were seven, the eighth being their dog.
3. Among the etiquette with Allah is that a servant should not say "I will do such and such in the future" without adding after it, "If Allah wills."
4. Among the etiquette: one who forgets the exception should make it even after some time. If he has sworn an oath, the exception does not benefit him unless it is connected to his speech.
5. Affirmation of the period the youths remained in their cave, which is three hundred and nine years by the lunar reckoning.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 27–31:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa-tlu ma ʾuḥiya ʾilayka mina al-kitab*: that is, recite the Qur'an in worship, in calling people (to God), and in teaching.

*Lā mubaddila li-kalimatihi*: that is, none can alter the words of God, in their wording, their meanings, or their rulings.

*Multaḥadan*: that is, a refuge toward which one inclines, seeking protection in it.

*Waṣbir nafsaka*: that is, restrain it.

*Yurīdūna wajhahu*: that is, seeking His obedience and His pleasure, not a passing good of this world.

*Wa-lā taʿdu ʿaynāka ʿanhum*: that is, do not let your gaze go past them to others from among the people of this world.

*Turīdu zīnata al-ḥayāt al-dunyā*: that is, by sitting with the rich you seek honor and pride.

*Man ʾaghfalnā qalbahu*: that is, We made his heart heedless of what he owes Us in remembrance and worship.

*Wa-kāna ʾamruhu furuṭan*: that is, loss and ruin.

*ʾAḥāṭa bihim surādiquhā*: a wall of fire surrounding these tormented ones in the Fire.

*Bi-māʾin ka-al-muhl*: that is, like the dregs of oil, the sediment that remains at the bottom of a vessel, thick and vile.

*Min sundusin wa-istabraq*: that is, what is thin of brocade; and istabraq is what is thick of it, that is, of brocade.

Explanation of the verses:

After the account of the People of the Cave, God commanded His Messenger to recite His Book, saying: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord﴾, that is, recite it in worship, in calling people to their Lord through it, and in teaching the believers the guidance it contains.

His saying: ﴿None can alter His words﴾ means: do not abandon its recitation, its practice, or its call, lest you become among the ruined, for what your Lord has promised to those who turn away from it and deny it is certainly true and surely comes to pass. Indeed your Lord ﴿none can alter His words﴾, which include His promise to His friends and His warning to His enemies among those who disbelieved and denied His Book, so they did not make lawful what He made lawful nor unlawful what He made unlawful.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you will not find besides Him any refuge﴾ means: if you do not recite His Book which He revealed to you and act by what is in it, what He threatened the disbelievers who turn away from His remembrance will befall you. ﴿And you will not find besides Him any refuge﴾, that is, a shelter to which you incline and a protection in which you seek safety. If such a severe warning is directed at the Messenger of God ﷺ, who is protected from error, then others who have abandoned the recitation of the Qur'an and acting upon it, neither upholding its limits nor making lawful its lawful nor unlawful its unlawful, are more deserving of this warning, and it will surely overtake them unless they repent before their death.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face﴾. This guidance was revealed to the Messenger ﷺ when the polytheists proposed that he remove his poor companions, such as Bilal and Suhayb and others, so that they might sit with him and listen to him. His Lord forbade him to do that and commanded him to restrain himself with those poor believers ﴿who call upon﴾ their Lord in their prayers in the morning and evening, not desiring by their prayer, their glorification, and their supplication any passing good of this world, but seeking the good pleasure and love of God through obedience to Him by night and day.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them﴾, that is, do not let your gaze go beyond these poor believers to those rich men, desiring to sit with them for honor and pride. And His saying: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾, that is, whom We made heedless of the remembrance of Us and of the mention of Our promise and Our warning, so that he would be among the ruined because of his obstinacy, arrogance, and wrongdoing.

﴿And his affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾, that is, loss and ruin.

His saying, Exalted is He, in the third verse of this passage: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve"﴾. That is, this which I have brought and to which I call, faith, monotheism, and obedience to God through righteous deeds, is ﴿the truth from your Lord﴾, O people. ﴿Whoever wills﴾, meaning whom God wills to guide, so he believes and does righteous deeds, He has saved him; and whom God does not will to guide, so he remains in his disbelief and does not believe, has indeed lost and failed.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose enclosure surrounds them﴾, that is, its fiery walls. ﴿And if they call for relief﴾ because of the severity of thirst, ﴿they will be relieved with water like molten brass﴾, vile and thick, ﴿which scalds the faces﴾; when the drinker brings it near his face to drink, it burns his skin and face, and therefore it is described as blameworthy. ﴿Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place﴾, that is, Hell, in its abode, its food, and its drink, for all of it is evil and torment. This is a warning to whoever chooses disbelief over faith. As for the promise to those who believed and did righteous deeds, which is contained in the two verses [31–32], God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, indeed We do not waste the reward of one who does good work﴾. This is Our decree which has no alteration. Then God explained their reward for their faith and the goodness of their deeds, saying: ﴿For them are gardens of perpetual residence﴾, that is, lasting abode, ﴿beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein upon thrones.﴾ The thrones are couches within canopies. Then God praised their blessing which He prepared for them, saying: ﴿How excellent the reward, and how good the resting place﴾, in its adornments, garments, furnishings, couches, food, drink, companions, and the pleasure of God therein. ﴿And how good a resting place it is﴾ in which they recline and enjoy. May God make us among its people.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the failure and loss of those who turn away from the Book of God, who neither recite it nor act upon the laws and rulings it contains.

2- Encouragement to sit with the people of the Hereafter, namely the poor who are patient, and abandoning the people of this world and turning away from what they are engaged in.

3- The one calling to God must make the truth clear, and people thereafter are according to what has been decreed for them or against them.

4- Encouragement and warning through mention of the reward of the two groups, the believers and the disbelievers.

5- The punishment of the Fire is the worst punishment, and the bliss of Paradise is the finest bliss; none perishes before God except one who is already doomed.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 32–38:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa-drib lahum mathalan* (And set forth for them an example): i.e., make for them an example: two men... etc.

*Jannatayn* (two gardens): i.e., two orchards.

*Wa-hafafnahuma bi-nakhl* (And We had surrounded them with date palms): i.e., We had encircled them with date palms.

*Ataat ukulaha* (Each of them yielded its produce): i.e., gave its fruit, which is what is eaten.

*Wa-lam tazlim minhu shay'an* (And did not fail in aught of it): i.e., did not diminish anything of it, but brought it forth complete and full.

*Khilalahuma nahran* (And We caused a river to gush forth within them): i.e., a flowing river through the trees and palms.

*Wa-huwa yuhawiruhu* (while he was conversing with him): i.e., speaking with him and talking to him.

*Wa-a'azz nafaran* (and more powerful in followers): i.e., in clan and kinsmen.

*Tabid* (perish): i.e., come to an end and pass away.

*Khayran minha munqalaban* (better in return): i.e., a better outcome (lit. return) in the Hereafter.

*A-kafarta billadhi khalaqaka min turab?!* (Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust?!): The interrogation is for reproach, and creation from dust is in terms of origin, namely Adam.

*Min nutfah* (from a drop): i.e., from semen.

*Thumma sawwaka* (then fashioned you): i.e., made you proportionate and made you a man.

*Lakinna* (But as for me): i.e., "lakin ana"; the alif was dropped and the nun assimilated into the nun, so it became *lakinna*.

*Huwa Allahu rabbi* (He is Allah, my Lord): i.e., I say, Allah is my Lord.

Meaning of the verses:

He, may He be exalted, says to His Messenger ﷺ: Set forth for those arrogant polytheists, who proposed to you that you drive away the poor believers from around you so that they might sit with you and hear from you, ﴿And set forth for them﴾, i.e., make for them an example: ﴿two men﴾, a believer and an unbeliever. ﴿We assigned to one of them﴾, namely the unbeliever, ﴿two gardens of grapevines, and We surrounded them with date palms﴾, i.e., We encircled them with date palms, ﴿and We placed between them﴾, i.e., between the vineyards and the palms, ﴿cultivated land﴾. ﴿Each of the two gardens yielded its produce and did not fail in aught of it﴾, i.e., did not diminish anything of it. ﴿And We caused a river to gush forth within them﴾ to water them. ﴿And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while conversing with him﴾, i.e., arguing and boasting to him in speech: ﴿I am greater than you in wealth and more powerful in followers﴾, i.e., in clan and kinsmen. He said this out of pride and arrogance. ﴿And he entered his garden while he was a wrongdoer to himself﴾ through disbelief and arrogance, and said: ﴿I do not think that this will ever perish﴾, pointing to his garden, ﴿ever﴾, i.e., will never come to an end. ﴿And I do not think the Hour will occur; and even if I should be returned to my Lord, as you claim, I will surely find better than this as a return﴾, i.e., a better outcome than my garden, if the Hour should occur, people be resurrected, and I be resurrected with them. This statement by this man is what is called the self-deception that afflicts the people of polytheism and arrogance. Here his companion, the Muslim, said to him, ﴿while he was conversing with him: Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust﴾, namely Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who created your father Adam from ﴿dust, then from a drop [of semen], then fashioned you as a man﴾. This is a reproach from the believer to the deluded unbeliever. Then he said to him: ﴿But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord﴾, i.e., but as for me, I say, Allah is my Lord, ﴿and I do not associate anyone with my Lord﴾ from His creation in worship.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The commendability of setting forth parables to bring hidden meanings to the minds.

2- A depiction of the ideal form of planting date palm and grape orchards.

3- Affirmation of the creed of monotheism, resurrection, and recompense.

4- Condemnation of arrogance and self-deception, which lead their possessor to polytheism and disbelief.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 39–44:

Explanation of the words:

*Ma shā’ Allāh* (what Allah wills): that is, it comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be.

*Ḥusbānan min al-samā’* (a reckoning from heaven): that is, a punishment cast down from the sky, so that it turns the garden into smooth ground, slippery, on which no foot can stand firm.

*Aw yuṣbiḥa māʾuhā ghawran* (or its water becomes sunken): that is, it sinks deep into the depths of the earth, so that one cannot draw it up or bring it out.

*Wa-uḥīṭa bi-thamarihi* (and its fruit was encompassed): that is, its fruit was destroyed, so that nothing of it remained.

*Yuqallibu kaffayhi* (he turns his palms over): in remorse and regret over the great effort and considerable wealth he had spent on it.

*Wa-hiya khāwiyatun ʿalā ʿurūshihā* (and it lies in ruins upon its trellises): that is, fallen upon its supports on which the vines were trained, and upon the walls of its buildings.

*Fiʾah* (a group): a body of people, strong like his clan among his people.

*Hunālika* (there): that is, when the punishment befell the owner of the two gardens, namely on the Day of Resurrection.

*Al-Walāyah* (authority): that is, the true dominion and sovereignty belong to Allah, the Exalted.

*Khayrun thawāban wa-khayrun ʿuqbā* (better in reward and better in outcome): that is, Allah, the Exalted, is the best of those who reward and the best of those who bring a good end, that is, He recompenses with good.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the parable of the poor believer and the rich disbeliever. The believer said to the disbeliever what Allah, the Exalted, reported in His words: ﴿And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say: "What Allah wills [has come to pass]; there is no power except with Allah"?﴾ That is, why did you not say, when you entered your garden and were amazed at its beauty and perfection, ﴿What Allah wills [has come to pass]﴾, meaning it came to be, ﴿there is no power except with Allah﴾, meaning no one has the power to do or leave anything except by Allah's enabling him and helping him to do it. He said this as counsel to the disbeliever and as a rebuke to him. Then he said to him: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children﴾ today, ﴿then perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden and send upon it﴾, that is, upon the disbeliever's garden, ﴿a reckoning from heaven﴾, that is, a punishment cast down. ﴿So that it becomes a smooth, slippery earth﴾: that is, dust, smooth, which produces no crops and on which no foot can stand firm. ﴿Or its water becomes sunken﴾, by which it is irrigated, sunk deep into the depths of the earth, so that you will not be able to draw it out again; this is the meaning of ﴿you will not be able to seek it [i.e., to find a way to it]﴾.

As for His words, in verses [40], [41], [42]: Allah, the Exalted, informs that the believer's hope was fulfilled, for the garden of the disbeliever was indeed encompassed, and so what was in it of fruit was destroyed. ﴿So he began to turn his palms over﴾ in remorse and regret ﴿over what he had spent upon it﴾ of effort and wealth in his garden, ﴿and it lay in ruins upon its trellises﴾, that is, fallen upon the supports of the vines on which he used to train them to bear them up, just as the walls of its buildings fell upon its roofs. He grieved and regretted and said: ﴿Would that I had not associated anyone with my Lord,﴾ ﴿and he had no group﴾ strong to help him ﴿besides Allah, nor was he one who could defend himself﴾, the one defeated, ﴿since whomever Allah forsakes has no helper.﴾ At the end of the parable Allah, the Exalted, said, ﴿There, it is a matter of the Walāyah [authority]﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the authority﴾, meaning the power, dominion and sovereignty, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾, that is, the true God, ﴿not to any other, such as idols and stones.﴾ ﴿He is the best in reward﴾, that is, the best to reward for faith and righteous deeds.

﴿And the best in outcome﴾, that is, the best to bring about an outcome, meaning He recompenses with good ends.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the destiny of the believers, such as Ṣuhayb, Salmān and Bilāl, which is Paradise, and the destiny of the disbelievers, such as Abū Jahl and ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, which is the Fire.

2- The recommendation that whoever is impressed by something say: ﴿What Allah wills [has come to pass]; there is no power except with Allah﴾, for he will then see nothing disliked in it, Allah willing.

3- Allah's response to His believing servants and the fulfilment of their hope in Him, glorified and exalted is He.

4- The one forsaken is the one whom Allah forsakes, for he will never be helped.

5- Walāyah in the sense of beneficial allegiance to the servant is allegiance to Allah, the Exalted, not allegiance to other than Him.

6- Walāyah in the sense of dominion and sovereignty belongs to Allah on the Day of Resurrection and not to anyone else, since both the dominion and the command belong to Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 45–46:

Explanation of the words:

Al-mathal (المثل): the striking attribute (al-sifah al-mu'jibah).

Hashiman (هشيماً): dry and crumbled.

Tadhruhu al-riyah (تذروه الرياح): the winds scatter it and disperse it because of its lightness and dryness.

Muqtadiran (مقتدراً): having complete power, nothing can overcome Him.

Zinat al-hayat al-dunya (زينة الحياة الدنيا): one adorns oneself with what is in it.

Al-baqiyat al-salihat (والباقيات الصالحات): these are the righteous deeds of all acts of worship and acts of drawing near to God.

Khayrun amalan (وخير أملاً): what a person hopes for and awaits of good.

Meaning of the verses:

This is another parable coined (madrub, i.e., made) for the life of this world, in which people were deceived and misled by it, and it diverted them from God, their Lord, so they did not remember Him and did not thank Him, and thus they deserved His anger and punishment.

God, the Exalted, said, addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And strike for them﴾, meaning for those deluded by wealth and power, ﴿the example of the life of this world﴾, meaning its true attribute, which never differs from it in any way: ﴿like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it﴾, so it flourishes, blooms, turns green and becomes beautiful, pleasing its owners and gladdening them with what they hope from it. Then suddenly the command of God comes upon it, with scorching, burning winds, ﴿and it becomes dry stubble﴾, meaning dry, shattered and broken, ﴿scattered by the winds﴾ here and there. ﴿And God is ever Able over all things﴾, meaning He is capable, with complete power; so the people of the world become despairing, hopeless of every good.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Wealth and children are adornment of the life of this world, but the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope﴾: after He had set forth the parable of the life of this world, which deceived its people and led them to the places of destruction, He informed them of another truth, by which He made His servants aware so that they might benefit from it. It is that ﴿wealth and children﴾, or the offspring, are ﴿adornment of the life of this world﴾ and nothing more, meaning one adorns oneself with them for a while, then they perish and go away. Therefore it is not permissible to be deceived by them, such that they become the chief concern of a person in this life and divert him from seeking the happiness of the Hereafter through faith and righteous deeds. This is the first part of the truth in this verse. The second part is that ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾, meaning acts of righteousness and kinds of worship, including ﴿Subhan Allah (Glory be to God), al-hamdu lillah (praise be to God), la ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but God), Allahu akbar (God is greatest), and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (there is no power nor strength except with God)﴾, these are ﴿better with your Lord for reward﴾, meaning recompense and fruits, which the servant gathers from continuous striving in pursuit of this world while turning away from seeking the Hereafter, ﴿and better for hope﴾, meaning what a person hopes for of good, wishes for and desires to attain.

Lessons of the verses:

1- Clarification of the baseness of this world and the evil of its end.

2- Affirmation that wealth and children are nothing more than adornment, and adornment is quick to vanish, and since they are so, it is not permissible to be deceived by them; the servant must seek what endures over what perishes, namely the enduring righteous deeds, of various kinds of goodness and acts of worship, such as prayer, remembrance, glorification, jihad, guarding the frontier (ribat), fasting and zakat.

Explanation of the words:

"Prostrate to Adam" (اسجدوا لآدم): i.e., honour him by prostrating to him, as I commanded you, in obedience to Me.

"Will you then take him and his offspring as allies?" (أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء؟): The question is one of denunciation. Allah, exalted is He, denounces the children of Adam for taking Satan and his offspring as allies who are obeyed and befriended with love and support, while they are an enemy to them. How strange is the state of the children of Adam, how do they do this!?

"Evil is it as a substitute for the wrongdoers" (بئس للظالمين بدلاً): Evil is the substitute of obeying Iblis and his offspring in place of obeying Allah and His Messenger.

"Misleaders as aides" (المضلين عضداً): i.e., I never took the devils, from among mankind and the jinn, as helpers in creation and governance, so how can you obey them and disobey Me?

"A place of perdition" (موبقاً): i.e., a valley of the valleys of Hell in which they will all be destroyed. This is when they enter the Fire. As for before it, al-Mawbiq is a barrier between the polytheists and what they used to worship, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are going to fall into it﴾.

"Going to fall into it" (مواقعوها): i.e., they will fall into it and will never leave it, ever.

"And they will not find from it any place of escape" (ولم يجدوا عنها مصرفاً): i.e., a place other than it to turn to in order to be saved from its punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in guiding the children of Adam and directing them to what saves them from punishment and achieves for them happiness in both abodes. Allah, exalted is He, says in addressing His Messenger: and mention to them ﴿when We said to the angels﴾, who are Our honoured servants, ﴿"Prostrate to Adam"﴾, so they complied with Our command and prostrated, except Iblis. But Iblis, whom people obey today, was of the jinn and not of the angels, and did not prostrate, and thus he defied Our command and departed from Our obedience. ﴿Will you then take him﴾, i.e., is it proper for you, O children of Adam, to take the enemy of your father, the enemy of your Lord, and also your enemy, as an ally whom you befriend, and his offspring, by obeying them and responding to what they ask of you of kinds of disbelief and wickedness? ﴿Evil is it as a substitute for the wrongdoers﴾ who wrong themselves: the obedience of Satan and his offspring and their guardianship in place of the obedience of Allah and His Messenger and their guardianship.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not have taken the misleaders as aides﴾ informs that He alone is the Creator and Governor; He has no specific minister. So how is Satan and his offspring worshipped, when I am the One who created them, and created the heavens and the earth, and created those who worship Satan? I did not ﴿take the misleaders﴾, who are the devils from among the jinn and mankind who mislead Our servants from Our path that leads to Our pleasure and Paradise, as helpers to me who support and strengthen My cause. The summary of what is in the verse is that Allah, exalted is He, denounces the people for worshipping the devils, which is obeying them, when they are created and He is the Creator of them and of everything.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will say, "Call those partners of Mine whom you claimed"﴾, i.e., mention, O Our Messenger, to these polytheists who turned away from worshipping Allah to worshipping His enemy Satan, mention to them the Day when it will be said to them on the plains of Resurrection: ﴿"Call those partners of Mine"﴾ whom you associated with Me in worship, claiming that they would intercede for you on this Day and save you from Our punishment.

Allah says: ﴿So they will call them﴾, "O so-and-so! O so-and-so!" ﴿but they will not respond to them﴾, for no one among those who were worshipped besides Allah will dare to say, "Lord, these used to worship me." Allah says: ﴿And We will put between them a barrier [mawbiq]﴾, i.e., a barrier and separation resulting from their enmity toward one another, and so that they do not connect with one another on the plains of Resurrection. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire﴾, i.e., it will be brought, dragged by chains, until it is displayed to the people of the standing place, and they will see it. At that moment the criminals will think, i.e., become certain, ﴿that they are going to fall into it﴾, i.e., they will enter it. ﴿And they will not find from it any place of escape﴾, i.e., a place they can turn to, because they will be surrounded by the angels of punishment, and we seek refuge in Allah from the Fire and its punishment.

From the guidance of the verses:

2- Wonder at the children of Adam: how they obey their enemy and disobey their Lord!

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 54–59:

Explanation of the words:

*Sarrafna* (We have varied): i.e., We have made clear and repeated the clarification.

*Min kulli mathal* (of every kind of example): *mathal* means a striking and wondrous attribute.

*Jadalan* (disputation): i.e., contention through speech.

*Sunnat al-awwalin* (the way of the earlier peoples): i.e., punishment by total annihilation and complete uprooting.

*Qubulan* (face to face): i.e., openly and visibly.

*Liyudhidu bihi al-haqq* (to refute the truth thereby): i.e., to nullify the truth by means of it.

*Huzuwan* (as a mockery): i.e., made an object of ridicule.

*Akinnah* (coverings): i.e., veils.

*Wa fi adhanihim waqran* (and heaviness in their ears): i.e., deafness, so that they do not hear.

*Mawilan* (a refuge): i.e., a place to which they can take shelter.

*Li-mahlikihim mawidan* (a fixed appointed time for their destruction): i.e., a specific time for their annihilation.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to explain the proofs of God Most High upon His servants, so that they may believe in Him, worship Him alone, be saved from His punishment, and enter the abode of His honor. God Most High said: ﴿And We have certainly varied in this Qur'an for the people from every kind of example﴾, i.e., We have struck in it many examples and clarified in it numerous proofs, ﴿We have varied in this Qur'an﴾ of promise and threat, to encourage and to warn, and they met all of that with denial and obstinacy, ﴿and mankind is ever most contentious of things﴾. Most of mankind spends its effort in disputation and contention, so that it does not submit to the truth, accept it, and fulfill its obligations toward it if it is incumbent upon them. This is what the first verse indicates [54]. As for the second verse, God Most High informs in it that nothing prevented people ﴿from believing when guidance came to them﴾, which is the explanation of the path of happiness and salvation through faith and righteous deeds after abandoning disbelief, polytheism and evil deeds, ﴿and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that there come to them the way of the earlier peoples﴾, namely the punishment of uprooting and total annihilation, ﴿or that there come to them﴾ the punishment of the Day of Resurrection face to face, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿or that the punishment come to them face to face﴾, and then faith will be of no benefit. And His words: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners﴾, i.e., guiding callers who give good tidings of Paradise to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and warn with the Fire those who disbelieve and do evil. We did not send them as tyrants, nor did We charge them with guiding all of mankind; but those who disbelieve turn away from this reality and dispute ﴿so that they may refute the truth thereby﴾. ﴿And they take﴾ the signs of God and His proofs ﴿and that with which they were warned﴾ of the punishment that is due for their disbelief and obstinacy, they take as mockery and ridicule, mocking and deriding it, and by this they have become among the most wrongdoing of people. This is what verse [57] established, when God Most High said in it: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who has been reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forward?﴾, i.e., of crime, evil and shirk. O God, truly there is no one more unjust than this disbelieving, stubborn human being. Then God Most High mentioned the cause of the injustice, turning away and forgetting of these wrongdoers who turn away and forget: it is that God, according to His custom toward whoever plunges deeply into evil, injustice and corruption, places veils upon his heart that encompass it, so that he comes to understand nothing; and He places heaviness in his ears so that he does not hear guidance. Therefore He said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, then, ever﴾, i.e., after He has placed veils upon their hearts and heaviness in their ears.

And His words: ﴿And your Lord is the Most Forgiving, Possessor of mercy. If He were to seize them for what they have earned﴾, i.e., if He were to take these wrongdoers who turn away to account for what they have earned, ﴿He would hasten for them the punishment﴾. But His forgiveness and mercy prevent that; otherwise He would hasten punishment for them and destroy them before your eyes while you look on.

But ﴿for them is an appointed time, and they will never find other than it a refuge﴾, a place to which they can turn, and no shelter to which they can flee. It is likely that this refers to the Day of Badr, because the context concerns the obstinate wrongdoers deprived of God's guidance, such as Abu Jahl, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq; this is the first point. Second, His words: ﴿And those cities — We destroyed them when they wronged﴾ refers to the people of the cities, the people of Hud, the people of Salih and the people of Lut. ﴿And We made for their destruction an appointed time﴾, i.e., for their destruction a specific fixed time; so likewise these criminals of Quraysh, whom He destroyed at Badr and cursed forever.

Guidance from the verses:

1- God Most High has left the people without excuse through the proofs He clarified in His Book and the examples He struck in it.

2- Clarification of the innate human inclination toward disputation and contention.

3- Clarification of the task of the messengers, which is giving good tidings and warning, not compelling people to believe.

4- Clarification of the great wrongdoing of one who is reminded by the Qur'an yet turns away, continuing his crimes and forgetting what his hands have put forward.

5- Clarification of God's custom that when a servant persists in evil and corruption, he is veiled from faith and good and deprived of guidance forever, until he dies in disbelief and wrongdoing and abides in the humiliating punishment.

**Explanation of the words:**

*"And when Musa said to his young man"*: meaning, remember when Musa ibn Imran, the prophet of the Children of Israel, said to his young man Yusha' ibn Nun ibn Afraim ibn Yusuf, peace be upon him.

*Majma' al-Bahrayn* (the meeting place of the two seas): that is, where the two seas met, the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome.

*Huqban* (a long period): *al-huqb* is a period of time, which is eighty years, and its plural is *ahqab*.

*Sabilahu fi al-bahri sarban* (his way into the sea, a tunnel): that is, his path into the sea, a tunnel-like passage.

*Fa-lamma jawaza* (when they had passed): that is, the place where the rock was, and from there the fish made its way into the sea, a tunnel.

*Fi al-bahri 'ajaban* (into the sea, in a marvelous way): that is, a marvel for Musa, as he was amazed at the fish being brought back to life and taking a path in the sea like a tunnel through a mountain.

*Qasasan* (retracing their steps): that is, they followed the traces of their footsteps.

*'Abdan min 'ibadina* (a servant from among Our servants): he is al-Khidr, peace be upon him.

*Mimma 'ullimta rushdan* (of what you have been taught, right guidance): that is, what leads to the truth and is a sign of guidance.

*Ma lam tuhit bihi khubran* (what you have not encompassed in knowledge): that is, knowledge.

*Wa la a'sli laka amran* (nor will I disobey you in any command): that is, I will comply with what you command me, even if it does not agree with my desires.

**Meaning of the verses:**

This is the story of Musa and al-Khidr, peace be upon them both, and it establishes and confirms the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). Such true narration cannot be recounted by anyone unless he receives it as revelation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Musa said﴾, that is, remember, O Our Messenger, as evidence of Our oneness, Our meeting, and your prophethood, when Musa ibn Imran, Our prophet to the Children of Israel, said to his young man Yusha' ibn Nun: ﴿I will not cease﴾, that is, I will keep traveling, ﴿until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾, where my Lord has guided me to meet a servant of His servants there who has more knowledge than I, so that I may learn from him knowledge that I can add to my own, ﴿or I will continue for a long time﴾, that is, I will keep going for a long period until I find this righteous servant and learn from him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then when they reached their meeting place﴾, that is, the meeting place of the two seas, which are the Sea of Rome and the Sea of Persia, at Bab al-Mandab, where the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean meet, or the Mediterranean and the Atlantic at Tangier. And Allah knows best which of them is meant. And His saying: ﴿They forgot their fish﴾, that is, the young man forgot the fish, since it was he who was carrying it. Yet the forgetting is attributed to both of them, in keeping with the familiar usage of the Arabic language. Allah the Exalted made this fish a sign for Musa of the presence of al-Khidr: the fish would be lost where he was. As related in al-Bukhari, the story begins with Musa delivering a sermon to the Children of Israel one day, which was eloquent and beneficial, and a young man among the Children of Israel was impressed by it and said to him: "Is there anyone more knowledgeable than you, O Musa?" He said: "No." So his Lord revealed to him immediately: "Yes, Our servant Khidr." His soul yearned to meet him and learn from him, so he asked his Lord for this, and He guided him to the place where he would meet him, the meeting place of the two seas, and made the fish a sign for him. He commanded him to take his food as a fish and informed him that when the fish was lost, there he would find the servant of Allah, Khidr. Hence, when they reached the meeting place of the two seas and rested, Musa slept and the young man was nearly asleep. Suddenly the fish came out of the *mikttal* (a container) and made its way to the sea, and the sea parted for it, becoming like an arch or a tunnel, a sign for Musa.

Sleep overcame Yusha', so he slept. When they had rested, they got up to continue their journey. The young man forgot, and the fish's exit from the container and entry into the sea slipped from his mind due to the overpowering sleep. When they had walked a considerable distance and felt hungry, having passed the place that was the meeting place of the two seas, Musa said to the young man: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾, and he gave the reason: ﴿Indeed, we have met with fatigue from this journey of ours﴾, that is, hardship. Here the young man replied to Musa with what Allah the Exalted related: he answered Musa, ﴿Do you remember?﴾, that is, do you recall ﴿when we took refuge at the rock﴾ where they had rested, ﴿for I forgot the fish﴾, and he spoke as one making an excuse, ﴿and none but Satan made me forget it, that I should mention it, and it took its way into the sea in a marvelous manner﴾, that is, it came back to life after death and went on until it reached the sea, and the sea parted for it so that it became a tunnel in it. Then Musa answered him with what Allah the Exalted related: ﴿He said: That is what we were seeking﴾, because Allah had made the loss of the fish a sign of the place where Khidr would be found. ﴿So they went back, retracing their steps﴾, that is, they returned ﴿following their footsteps﴾, meaning they tracked the traces of their feet. ﴿And they found﴾ Khidr, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they found a servant from among Our servants﴾, who was Khidr, ﴿whom We had given mercy from Us﴾, that is, prophethood, ﴿and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾, which is a special knowledge of the unseen known only to him.

﴿Musa said to him﴾, seeking his favor: ﴿May I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, as right guidance?﴾, that is, of what Allah has taught you as guidance, a path that guides me to the truth and through which I may attain true guidance. Al-Khidr answered him with what Allah the Exalted related: ﴿He said: Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me﴾, meaning that he would see from him things that he would not approve of, and Khidr would necessarily do them, so Musa would be distressed by that and would not be able to bear patience. He gave him the reason for his inability to be patient in his saying: ﴿And how can you be patient about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾, that is, complete knowledge. Musa answered him, having resolved to undertake the journey in search of knowledge whatever the cost, and said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any command﴾, that is, I will comply with what you command me, even if it is not in accordance with what I love and desire.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Allah the Exalted rebuked His messenger Musa, peace be upon him, when he was asked whether there was anyone more knowledgeable than him and he said "No," whereas he should have said at least "Allah knows best." For this, he was punished by being assigned this arduous journey.

2. It is recommended to keep company on a journey, and for a student to serve his teacher, as Yusha' used to serve Musa by carrying the provisions.

3. Forgetfulness befalls a person, however righteous he may be.

4. Returning to what is right after making a mistake is better than persisting in error. ﴿So they went back, retracing their steps﴾?

5. The manifestation of Allah's power in bringing the fish back to life after death, and the parting of the water over it until it became like an arch, so that it was a tunnel for the fish and a marvel for Musa and his young man.

Musa thereby deduced the location of Khidr through this marvel, and he found him there.

6. It is recommended to seek more knowledge, however learned a person may be. Here I cite the following hadith, which is better than a qintar (a large measure) of gold for one who memorizes it and acts upon it, and this is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Musa asked his Lord: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is most just?" He said: "The one who judges by the truth and does not follow his desires." He said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most knowledgeable?" He said: "The one who seeks the knowledge of people in addition to his own knowledge, perhaps he will obtain a word that guides him to guidance or turns him away from ruin." The remainder of this report is mentioned by Ibn Jarir in his commentary on these verses.

*Majma' al-Bahrayn* (the meeting place of the two seas): that is, where the two seas met, the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome.

*Huqban* (a long period): *al-huqb* is a period of time, which is eighty years, and its plural is *ahqab*.

*Sabilahu fi al-bahri sarban* (his way into the sea, a tunnel): that is, his path into the sea, a tunnel-like passage.

*Fa-lamma jawaza* (when they had passed): that is, the place where the rock was, and from there the fish made its way into the sea, a tunnel.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 70–74:

Explanation of the words:

Dhikran (ذكراً): i.e., an explanation and detailed account of what remained hidden from you.

Laqad ji'ta shay'an imra (لقد جئت شيئاً إمراً): i.e., you have done a reprehensible thing.

La turhiqni (لا ترهقني): i.e., do not burden me with what is difficult for me and beyond my capacity to bear, so that my companionship with you becomes straitened for me.

Nafsan zakiyyah (نفساً زكية): i.e., pure, whose soul has not been soiled by sins.

Bi-ghayri nafs (بغير نفس): i.e., without retaliation (qisas).

Nukran (نكراً): a matter that the revealed laws and the intellects deny, of all kinds of wrongs; it is the extremely abhorrent wrong.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the dialogue between Musa (peace be upon him) and the scholar whom he wished to accompany in order to seek knowledge from him, who was al-Khidr. The words of the Most High: ﴿He said﴾, i.e., al-Khidr, ﴿"If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything﴾ that I do, of which you do not know a legitimate reason, ﴿until I myself mention to you its explanation﴾, i.e., until I myself be the one who clarifies to you its reality and what you did not know of it. And the words of the Most High: ﴿So they set out﴾, i.e., after Musa agreed to al-Khidr's request, they set out, traveling on the earth, until they reached a seaport, and boarded a ship whose owners al-Khidr knew, so they did not take a fare from them for the passage. When the ship sailed and went out into the sea, al-Khidr took an axe and made a hole in the ship. Musa began stuffing the hole with a cloth of his and said: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people?"﴾ [saying that] they had carried us without a fare. ﴿"You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ That is, "You have done, O scholar, an abominable wrong." Al-Khidr answered him with what the Most High related: ﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ Musa answered with what the Most High mentioned of him: ﴿"Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair."﴾ That is, "Do not punish me for forgetting, for the forgetful one bears no blame." This was genuine forgetfulness on Musa's part, and "do not burden me with what is difficult for me and I cannot bear, so that I become straitened in my companionship with you."

The Most High said: ﴿So they set out﴾ after their descent from the sea to the land, and they found a boy, handsome and beautiful, playing with the boys. Al-Khidr took him aside, laid him down and slaughtered him. Musa said to him, as the Most High related: ﴿"Have you killed a pure soul without its having killed anyone?"﴾ Pure (zakiyyah), i.e., clean, whose owner had not committed a sin that would soil his soul, and had not killed a person for which he deserved retaliation. ﴿"You have certainly done a dreadful thing!"﴾ That is, you have committed an abominable wrong by killing a pure soul that had not sinned. This was not forgetfulness on Musa's part; rather it was deliberate, for he could not bear to witness such an abominable act for which he knew no justification or cause.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The permissibility of making conditions in companionship, seeking knowledge, and other matters for a predominant benefit.

2- The permissibility of boarding ships at sea.

3- The legitimacy of denouncing wrongdoing toward one who is known to be doing wrong.

4- The lifting of hardship from people.

5- The legitimacy of retaliation (qisas): a life for a life.
