The noble context continues with the dialogue between Musa (peace be upon him) and the scholar whom he wished to accompany in order to seek knowledge from him, who was al-Khidr. The words of the Most High: ﴿He said﴾, i.e., al-Khidr, ﴿"If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything﴾ that I do, of which you do not know a legitimate reason, ﴿until I myself mention to you its explanation﴾, i.e., until I myself be the one who clarifies to you its reality and what you did not know of it. And the words of the Most High: ﴿So they set out﴾, i.e., after Musa agreed to al-Khidr's request, they set out, traveling on the earth, until they reached a seaport, and boarded a ship whose owners al-Khidr knew, so they did not take a fare from them for the passage. When the ship sailed and went out into the sea, al-Khidr took an axe and made a hole in the ship. Musa began stuffing the hole with a cloth of his and said: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people?"﴾ [saying that] they had carried us without a fare. ﴿"You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ That is, "You have done, O scholar, an abominable wrong." Al-Khidr answered him with what the Most High related: ﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ Musa answered with what the Most High mentioned of him: ﴿"Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair."﴾ That is, "Do not punish me for forgetting, for the forgetful one bears no blame." This was genuine forgetfulness on Musa's part, and "do not burden me with what is difficult for me and I cannot bear, so that I become straitened in my companionship with you."

The Most High said: ﴿So they set out﴾ after their descent from the sea to the land, and they found a boy, handsome and beautiful, playing with the boys. Al-Khidr took him aside, laid him down and slaughtered him. Musa said to him, as the Most High related: ﴿"Have you killed a pure soul without its having killed anyone?"﴾ Pure (zakiyyah), i.e., clean, whose owner had not committed a sin that would soil his soul, and had not killed a person for which he deserved retaliation. ﴿"You have certainly done a dreadful thing!"﴾ That is, you have committed an abominable wrong by killing a pure soul that had not sinned. This was not forgetfulness on Musa's part; rather it was deliberate, for he could not bear to witness such an abominable act for which he knew no justification or cause.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The permissibility of making conditions in companionship, seeking knowledge, and other matters for a predominant benefit.

2- The permissibility of boarding ships at sea.

3- The legitimacy of denouncing wrongdoing toward one who is known to be doing wrong.

4- The lifting of hardship from people.

5- The legitimacy of retaliation (qisas): a life for a life.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 75–78:

Explanation of the words:

"He said: Did I not tell you": that is, Khadir said to Musa, peace be upon them both.

"After this": that is, after this time.

"Then do not accompany me": that is, do not leave me to follow you.

"Excuse from my side": that is, from my direction, an excuse for not accompanying you.

"The people of a town": the city of Antioch.

"Asked its people for food": that is, they asked them for the food that is due to a guest.

"About to collapse": that is, it was close to falling because it was leaning.

"Then he set it upright": that is, Khadir, meaning he repaired it so that it would not fall.

"A wage": that is, a payment for its repair and restoration.

"This is the parting between me and you": that is, your saying, "If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it," is the end of the companionship and the beginning of separation.

"With an interpretation": that is, an explanation of what you denied, according to your knowledge.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the dialogue of Khadir with Musa, peace be upon them both. Musa's denunciation of Khadir's killing of the boy without a soul was mentioned earlier, and he had committed it without doubt, and Musa exaggerated in his denunciation until he said: ﴿Indeed, you have done a thing terrible⦆ [al-Kahf: 74]. Khadir answered him with what Allah, the Exalted, related in His saying: ﴿Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?⦆, when you asked me for companionship for instruction. Musa answered with what Allah, the Exalted, related in His saying: ﴿[Musa] said, "If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have already received an excuse from me.⦆ That is: "after this time." ﴿Then do not keep me as a companion⦆ means: leave my companionship, for you have ﴿already received an excuse from me⦆, that is, from my direction and before me, for your leaving me.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they set out⦆ on their journey ﴿until, when they came to the people of a town⦆ ["that is, a city"]. It is said it was Antioch, and they reached it at night, and the weather was cold, ﴿and they asked its people for food⦆, that is, they asked them for the food due to a guest, ﴿but they refused to entertain them. And they found therein a wall about to collapse⦆, that is, in the town, ﴿so [Khadir] set it upright⦆, meaning Khadir repaired it and made it upright. Musa said to him: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it⦆, that is, a payment in return for its repair, especially since the people of this town did not give us our due of hospitality. Here Khadir said to Musa: ﴿This is the parting between me and you⦆, because you pledged that if you asked me about anything after the incident of the killing of the boy, you would not seek my companionship, and now you have asked me; so this is the time of your parting. ﴿I will inform you⦆, that is, I will tell you ﴿of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience⦆: the tearing of the ship, the killing of the boy, and the setting up of the wall.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to fulfil what a person has pledged to another.

2- The obligation of hospitality towards one who deserves it.

3- The permissibility of giving charity in any good or work seeking the Face of Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 79–82:

Explanation of the words:

al-masakin (the needy): plural of miskin, the weak one unable to earn a living.

ya'malun fi al-bahr (they work on the sea): that is, they hire out their ship to passengers.

a'ibaha (I would make it defective): that is, I would make it faulty so that no one would desire it.

ghasban (by force): that is, by compulsion.

an yurhiqahuma tughyanan wa kufran (that he would overwhelm them with rebellion and disbelief): that is, that he would cover them with wrongdoing and denial.

wa aqraba ruhma (and nearer in mercy): that is, in compassion, since ruhm (womb/kinship) and rahma (mercy) have the same root meaning.

wa ma fa'altuhu 'an amri (and I did not do it of my own accord): that is, not by my own choice, but by the command of my Lord, may His majesty be exalted and His authority be great.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the end of the account of Musa and al-Khadir, peace be upon them. When al-Khadir announced his parting from Musa, he had promised to explain to him the interpretation of what he could not bear with patience. Here is his explanation, related by Allah the Exalted as the words of al-Khadir: ﴿As for the ship﴾, which I damaged and you disapproved of, ﴿it belonged to needy people who work on the sea﴾, hiring out their ship to earn some sustenance, ﴿so I wished to make it defective﴾, not to drown its people, ﴿and behind them was a king﴾, a tyrant, ﴿who seizes every ship﴾ that is sound ﴿by force﴾, that is, by compulsion. I only wished to preserve it for them, since that king takes only sound ships. ﴿As for the boy﴾ whom I killed and you disapproved of my killing, ﴿his parents were believers, and we feared﴾ that if he grew up ﴿he would overwhelm them﴾, that is, cover them, ﴿with rebellion and disbelief. So we wished that their Lord would replace him with one better than him in purity﴾, that is, in cleanliness and righteousness, ﴿and nearer in mercy﴾, that is, in compassion and kindness toward them; therefore I killed him. ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord desired that they should reach their maturity﴾, that is, the age of discernment, ﴿and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord﴾, that is, that was a mercy. ﴿And I did not do it of my own accord﴾, that is, not by my own will and choice, but it was by the command of my Lord and His instruction. ﴿That is﴾, this is ﴿the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Demonstration of various kinds of the hidden kindnesses of Allah the Exalted; so the believer must be content with the decree of Allah, even if its outward appearance seems harmful.

2- Demonstration of the excellent management of Allah the Exalted toward His friends, through what outwardly appears as punishment but inwardly contains mercy.

3- Attention to the righteousness of parents in the reform of their children's condition.

4- Everything al-Khadir did was by divine revelation, and it is not of what the ignorant people claim and call "the knowledge of the unseen" (al-'ilm al-ladunni), which they attribute to those whom they call the saints; they sometimes call it "unveiling" (kashf). What refutes this claim is that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Al-Khadir said to Musa: 'I am upon a knowledge that Allah taught me, and you are upon a knowledge that Allah taught you,' and my knowledge and your knowledge compared to the knowledge of Allah is no more than what a bird takes with its beak from the sea."

The question that Quraysh put to the Prophet (ﷺ) was prompted by the Jews of Madinah, who told Quraysh: "Ask him about the Spirit, the People of the Cave, and Dhu al-Qarnayn. If he answers you, then he is a prophet; otherwise, he is not a prophet, so form your own judgment of him." The answer about the Spirit came in Surat al-Isra', and the answer about the youths and Dhu al-Qarnayn came in this Surah, Surat al-Kahf. The detailed account of the People of the Cave was given earlier in the beginning of the Surah, and this is the beginning of the account containing the answer about the king Dhu al-Qarnayn (peace be upon him).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They ask you, O our Prophet, about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say:﴾ to the questioners from the polytheists of Quraysh, ﴿"I will recite to you a report about him"﴾, i.e., I will read to you from his affair and his great story a report that carries admonition, knowledge and understanding.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We established him in the land and gave him from every thing a means﴾ — this is the beginning of the account about him. Allah the Exalted informs us that He established him in the land with kingship and authority, and gave him from everything he needed in conquering the land and spreading justice and goodness in it a means that would lead him to that. His saying ﴿so he followed a means﴾ follows the way of Allah in the perfection of things: whoever makes a needle and follows the means by which the needle is made will make a larger tool. Likewise, he followed a chain of means: warfare, conquest and travel through the land. ﴿Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring﴾, which lies on the coast of the Atlantic Ocean. Its setting there is according to the appearance to the eye; otherwise the sun is in the sky, while the muddy spring and the ocean are beside it on the earth.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And he found near it﴾, i.e., near that spring in that western region, ﴿a people﴾, i.e., disbelievers who were not Muslims. Allah permitted him to exercise control and authority over them, since He made the means of victory over them easy for him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿We said, "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either punish them or treat them with kindness."﴾ It may be that he was a prophet and that this saying of Allah was a revelation to him. The choice is ﴿either punish them﴾ by capture and killing, ﴿or take them with kindness﴾, and this was after the war with them and his victory over them. Dhu al-Qarnayn answered his Lord with what Allah the Exalted related: ﴿As for whoever does wrong﴾, i.e., by associating partners with Allah and disbelieving, ﴿we will punish him﴾ by killing and capture, ﴿then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ after his death, ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾, i.e., a dreadful, painful one.

﴿But as for whoever believes and does righteousness﴾, i.e., accepts Islam and makes his Islam good, ﴿he will have a reward, the best﴾ for his faith and his good deeds, i.e., Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿And We will speak to him of Our command with ease﴾, so We will not be harsh with him in speech, nor burden him with what is hard for him and overwhelms him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then he followed a means﴾, i.e., with the power he had obtained by conquering the west, he employed it to continue conquest in the east, ﴿until, when he reached the rising place of the sun, he found it rising over a people﴾ who were primitive, whom the land on which they lived had not helped to become civilized. Therefore they do not build houses or wear clothes, but live in caves, grottoes and underground tunnels. This is what His saying indicates: ﴿for whom We had not made any shelter from it﴾, i.e., from the sun. His saying: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., the statement We have made and the description We have given you of the state of Dhu al-Qarnayn, ﴿and We encompassed what was with him﴾ of power, material and spiritual means, ﴿in knowledge﴾, i.e., with complete knowledge.

His saying: ﴿Then he followed a means﴾, i.e., Dhu al-Qarnayn ﴿followed a means﴾, i.e., he continued on his path of warfare and conquest, ﴿until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾, which are two mountains at the farthest northeast of the earth. Dhu al-Qarnayn built between them a great barrier that prevented Ya'juj and Ma'juj from raiding the region adjacent to them. They are the people about whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿he found beside them a people who could hardly understand speech﴾, so they could not understand what was said to them and were addressed only with great difficulty and great slowness.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. Confirmation of the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), since this is the answer to the third of Quraysh's questions. He recited it to them as a Qur'an revealed to him.

2. Following one means after another, by which a person of sound judgment and will reaches the achievement of what is like miracles.

3. The statement of Dhu al-Qarnayn: ﴿As for whoever does wrong…etc.﴾ should be a constitutional principle by which individuals and groups are governed, because of its truthfulness, its beneficial character, and its agreement with the judgment and pleasure of Allah the Exalted. It is regrettable that this sound statement and rightful ruling are reversed, so that the people of wrongdoing become honored by governments, while the people of faith and steadfastness are humiliated!!

4. A demonstration that primitive peoples existed even after the time of Dhu al-Qarnayn, who wore no clothing and lived only in caves and grottoes. Even now there are tribes in the African lands who wear no clothes, but put threads and straps only over their private parts.

5. A confirmation that this righteous king ruled the earth, and he is one of the four who governed mankind in the east and the west.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 94–101:

Explanation of the words:

Ya'juj wa-Ma'juj (Gog and Magog): two tribes from the descendants of Yafith ibn Nuh (peace be upon him), and Allah knows best.

Kharjan (a payment): i.e., a fee in return for work.

Saddan (a barrier): as-sadd, with a fatha or a damma, is the barrier that prevents one thing from another.

Radman (a strong barrier): a fortified barrier, which is the same as a sadd.

Zubar al-hadid (blocks of iron): plural of zubrah, a piece of iron the size of the stone with which one builds.

Bayn as-sadafayn (between the two cliffs): i.e., the two sides of the two mountains.

Qitran (molten copper): al-qitr is molten copper.

Fama istaza'u an yazharuh (they could not scale it): i.e., they were unable to climb over it because of its height and smoothness.

Naqban (a breach): i.e., making an opening beneath it through which they could pass.

Ja'alahu dakkan (He made it level): i.e., dust level with the ground.

Wa-taraknا ba'dahum (And We left some of them): i.e., Ya'juj and Ma'juj, who go and come in agitation like the waves of the sea.

A'yunuhum fi ghita' 'an dhikri (Their eyes were under a covering from My remembrance): i.e., from the Qur'an; they do not open their eyes to what you recite to them, out of hatred for it. Or it means the eyes of their hearts, which are their insight; they are under coverings and do not perceive or recognize the truth.

La yastati'un sam'an (They could not bear to hear): because of their hatred of the truth and of the one who calls to it.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the account of Dhu al-Qarnayn, when the inhabitants of the north-eastern region of the earth complained to him about what Allah, the Exalted, had told of them when He said: ﴿They said, "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj are corrupters in the land"﴾, meaning by killing, eating, destroying and ruining. ﴿So may we pay you a tribute on the condition that you place between us and them a barrier?﴾ meaning a strong barrier through which they cannot reach us. Dhu al-Qarnayn answered them with what Allah the Exalted related in His saying: ﴿He said, "That in which my Lord has established me is better"﴾ of wealth, power and authority, ﴿[so] help me with strength, and I will make between you and them a barrier﴾, meaning a strong dam and a preventing barrier. ﴿Bring me sheets of iron﴾, meaning pieces of iron, each piece like a brick laid down. So they brought them to him, and he began placing the stones and blocks of iron and building until the construction rose and leveled the space between the two cliffs, the two sides of the mountains. He said to them, ﴿Blow,﴾ meaning blow the fire upon the iron, ﴿until when he made it [red as] fire, he said, "Bring me molten copper to pour over it."﴾ So they brought it to him, and he poured over it of the molten copper until it became like a single sheet of copper. ﴿So they [i.e., Ya'juj and Ma'juj] were unable to scale it﴾, ﴿nor could they make a breach through it.﴾ When he looked at it, a towering mountain and an impregnable fortress, he said, "This is a mercy from my Lord," meaning a result of the mercy of my Lord upon me and upon the people. And he added, ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level,﴾ which is the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj near the Hour, ﴿and the promise of my Lord is ever true.﴾ This is among what He promised, and it will certainly occur. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We will leave them that day surging over one another,﴾ meaning mixed together and in turmoil, both mankind and jinn. ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a comprehensive gathering﴾ for reckoning and recompense. ﴿And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, exposed,﴾ a real exposure, in which they see it up close. Then He mentioned the sin of the disbelievers and the reason for their being presented to the Fire, saying: and His true word: ﴿Those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance,﴾ meaning the eyes of their hearts, which are their insight, so they do not look at the signs of Allah in creation to be guided by them to the existence of Allah and the obligation of worshipping Him and His oneness, nor at the Qur'anic signs to be guided by them to the fact that there is no god but Allah, and to worship Him in the manner contained in the Qur'anic verses. ﴿And they were not able to hear﴾ the truth and what the messengers of Allah called to of guidance and goodness.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of a paid fee (ju'alah) for carrying out tasks.

2- The virtue of volunteering one's physical and mental effort.

3- The legitimacy of cooperating in what is good or in averting evil.

4- Affirmation of the existence of the nation of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and that their emergence is among the signs of the Hour.

5- Affirmation of the Resurrection and recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 102–106:

Explanation of the words:

Afa-hasiba alladhina kafaru: The interrogative is for rebuke and reproach.

An yattakhidhu ibadi: such as the angels, Jesus son of Mary, Uzair (Ezra), and others.

Awliya': lords whom they worship with various kinds of worship.

Nuzulan: the nuzul (an entertainment prepared for a guest), which is his food, drink, and lodging.

Dalla sa'yuhum: that is, their deeds became void and corrupt for them, so they gained nothing from them.

Yuhsinuna sun'an: that is, by a deed for which they would be rewarded with good and a fine recompense.

Bi-ayati rabbihim: that is, by the Qur'an and what it contains of proofs of monotheism and legal rulings.

Wa-liqa'ihi: that is, they disbelieved in the Resurrection and the recompense.

Waznan: that is, We will not give them any rank or value; rather We will despise and humiliate them.

Dhalika: that is, those—their recompense is Hell. The word "dhalika" (that) was used in place of "ulaika" (those), because, through their disbelief and the nullification of their deeds, they became like foam of the torrent, with no good in it and no weight, so it was fitting to point to them with "that."

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted addresses the polytheists, denouncing their polytheism and rebuking them, reproaching them for their supposition that taking His servants besides Him as allies whom they worship—such as the angels, whom some Arabs worshipped; the Messiah, whom the Christians worshipped; and Uzair, whom some Jews worshipped—would not anger Him, nor would He punish them for it. And how would He not be angered by it and not punish them for it, when He has prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a nuzul, that is, a house of hospitality, in which is their food, their drink, and their bedding, as the Exalted said: ﴿For them there will be a bed of Hell, and above them coverings [of fire]﴾ [Al-A'raf: 41]. This is what the first verse [102] indicates, which is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors instead of Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.﴾

As for His words in the second verse [103], the Exalted informs, using the interrogative style to create eagerness for the news, saying: ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾ O believers, ﴿those whose effort is lost in the worldly life while they think they are doing good work﴾, that is, a deed. He identifies them, saying: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾, so they did not believe in them, and in the meeting with their Lord, so they did not do the deed that would make Him pleased with them and make them happy, which is correct faith and righteous deeds that Allah legislated for His believing servants, by which they draw near to Him. Therefore their deeds were nullified, because they were shirk, disbelief, evil, and corruption. ﴿So We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾, since there is no value for them nor for their polytheistic, corrupt, and false deeds, for indeed one of them does not weigh the wing of a mosquito due to his lightness.

Finally, the Exalted announced His judgment concerning them and upon them, saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, the aforementioned foam of creation, ﴿their recompense is Hell﴾, and He gave the reason for the judgment, saying: ﴿because they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in mockery﴾, that is, because of their disbelief and their mockery of the signs of their Lord and His messengers. So the judgment was just, and the recompense was fitting, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the shirk of one who takes the angels, the prophets, or the saints as gods to be worshipped, under the slogan of drawing near to Allah, seeking intercession through them, and seeking nearness to Allah through love of them and drawing close to them.

2- Affirmation of the ruin of the people of desires who worship Allah in ways not legislated and seek nearness to Him by means other than those He made a means to His pleasure and Paradise, such as the Kharijites, the monks of the Christians, the innovating Rafidah, the Isma'iliyyah, the Nusayriyyah, the Druze, and others like them among the extremist innovators in beliefs, acts of worship, and legal rulings.

3- A deed that does not accord with Allah's pleasure and acceptance has no value, no weight, and no measure, whereas a deed that is weighed with Allah belongs to its doer, even if he dies in fear of Allah or in longing for Him.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 18, verses 107–110:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Kanat lahum* (they shall have): i.e., the reward of their faith and their righteous deeds.

*Al-Firdaws nuzulan* (the Firdaws as a dwelling): it is the middle of Paradise and its highest part, and *nuzulan* means a place of honour and bounty.

*La yabghuna 'anha hiwalan* (they will not desire any change from it): i.e., they will not seek a transfer from it, because there is nothing better than it, ever.

*Law kana al-bahru* (if the sea were): i.e., its water were ink.

*Qabla an tanfada kalimat Rabbi* (before the words of my Lord are exhausted): i.e., before they are finished.

*La-nafida al-bahru* (the sea would be exhausted): i.e., and the words would not be exhausted, that is, would not be finished.

*Yarju liqa'a Rabbihi* (hopes for the meeting with his Lord): he hopes for and awaits the resurrection and the recompense on the Day of Resurrection, when he will meet his Lord, exalted is He.

*Wa la yushrik bi-'ibadati Rabbihi ahadan* (and does not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord): i.e., he does not show off his deed to anyone, nor associate anyone with God, exalted is He, in worship.

**The meaning of the verses:**

After Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the recompense of the people of polytheism and desires, which is Hell, it was fitting to mention the recompense of the people of faith and piety, which consists of doing righteous deeds and avoiding what is forbidden. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning they affirmed the truth of Allah and His Messenger, believed in the meeting with Allah, and in His promise to His friends and His threat to His enemies among the people of polytheism and sins; and they did righteous deeds, performing the obligatory duties and obligations and hastening to the voluntary acts and good works. These ﴿shall have﴾ in the knowledge and decree of Allah ﴿the Gardens of Firdaws﴾, meaning gardens of Firdaws as a dwelling they will take up, and an abode of honour in which they will be honoured and blessed. Firdaws is the highest and middle part of Paradise. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, describing it and encouraging towards it, and having ascended to a level above it on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj, said: "If you ask Allah, then ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and its highest part, and above it is the Throne of the Merciful, blessed and exalted is He, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth," as in the Sahih. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Therein they will abide forever; they will not desire any change from it﴾, meaning they will remain in it forever, not seeking any transfer from it, since its bliss never wearies, its happiness never diminishes, its purity is never clouded, and its joy is never marred by death, sickness, fatigue, or toil. May Allah make us and whoever says "Amin" among its people. Amin.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement."﴾ This verse contains a refutation of the Jews, who, when the saying of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little﴾ [al-Isra': 85] was revealed, argued against it, when they were asked about the soul through a delegation of Quraysh sent to them. They said: "We have been given the Torah, and in it is the knowledge of everything." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: "Say: If the sea were ink..." as a refutation of them and an invalidation of their claims. He informed them, and informed everyone who claims knowledge, that there is no knowledge beyond it, that even if the water of the sea were ink, and every branch and stick in all the trees of the world were a pen, and they wrote with them, the water of the sea and the branches of the trees would be exhausted, while the words of my Lord, which carry the divine sciences and knowledge, indicate it and guide to it, would not be exhausted. Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah the Mighty; glory be to Allah, to whom the knowledge of everything has come to its end, and He is over all things competent.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God."﴾ Allah, exalted is He, commands His Messenger to say to the polytheists who ask him for miracles like those given to Moses and Jesus: "I am only a human being like you; I am not able to do what you are not able to do. The difference between us is that it is revealed to me the matter from my Lord, and it is not revealed to you. It is revealed to me that your God, i.e., your true object of worship and your truthful Lord, is one God: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old." And His saying ﴿So whoever hopes﴾, i.e., aspires and awaits ﴿for the meeting with his Lord﴾, out of fear of Him and desire for Him, ﴿let him do righteous deeds﴾ while being a believer, certain, ﴿and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, for polytheism nullifies and invalidates deeds. By this, his hope is sincere and his expectation is righteous and correct.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.
2. Explanation of the best of gardens, which is the highest Firdaws.
3. The knowledge of Allah is infinite, because His words are infinite.
4. Affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, exalted is He.
5. Affirmation of the humanity of the Prophet ﷺ, and that he is not merely a spirit or a light, as the extremist Batiniyya say.
6. Affirmation of monotheism and condemnation of polytheism.
7. Affirmation that showing off is polytheism, since it is reported that the verse was revealed to explain the ruling on a person who strives while desiring the face of Allah but also wishing to be seen in his place among people, who prays and fasts and loves to be praised for that.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Kanat lahum* (they shall have): i.e., the reward of their faith and their righteous deeds.

*Al-Firdaws nuzulan* (the Firdaws as a dwelling): it is the middle of Paradise and its highest part, and *nuzulan* means a place of honour and bounty.

*La yabghuna 'anha hiwalan* (they will not desire any change from it): i.e., they will not seek a transfer from it, because there is nothing better than it, ever.

*Law kana al-bahru* (if the sea were): i.e., its water were ink.

*Qabla an tanfada kalimat Rabbi* (before the words of my Lord are exhausted): i.e., before they are finished.

*La-nafida al-bahru* (the sea would be exhausted): i.e., and the words would not be exhausted, that is, would not be finished.

*Yarju liqa'a Rabbihi* (hopes for the meeting with his Lord): he hopes for and awaits the resurrection and the recompense on the Day of Resurrection, when he will meet his Lord, exalted is He.

*Wa la yushrik bi-'ibadati Rabbihi ahadan* (and does not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord): i.e., he does not show off his deed to anyone, nor associate anyone with God, exalted is He, in worship.

**The meaning of the verses:**

After Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the recompense of the people of polytheism and desires, which is Hell, it was fitting to mention the recompense of the people of faith and piety, which consists of doing righteous deeds and avoiding what is forbidden. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning they affirmed the truth of Allah and His Messenger, believed in the meeting with Allah, and in His promise to His friends and His threat to His enemies among the people of polytheism and sins; and they did righteous deeds, performing the obligatory duties and obligations and hastening to the voluntary acts and good works. These ﴿shall have﴾ in the knowledge and decree of Allah ﴿the Gardens of Firdaws﴾, meaning gardens of Firdaws as a dwelling they will take up, and an abode of honour in which they will be honoured and blessed. Firdaws is the highest and middle part of Paradise. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, describing it and encouraging towards it, and having ascended to a level above it on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj, said: "If you ask Allah, then ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and its highest part, and above it is the Throne of the Merciful, blessed and exalted is He, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth," as in the Sahih. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Therein they will abide forever; they will not desire any change from it﴾, meaning they will remain in it forever, not seeking any transfer from it, since its bliss never wearies, its happiness never diminishes, its purity is never clouded, and its joy is never marred by death, sickness, fatigue, or toil. May Allah make us and whoever says "Amin" among its people. Amin.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement."﴾ This verse contains a refutation of the Jews, who, when the saying of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little﴾ [al-Isra': 85] was revealed, argued against it, when they were asked about the soul through a delegation of Quraysh sent to them. They said: "We have been given the Torah, and in it is the knowledge of everything." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: "Say: If the sea were ink..." as a refutation of them and an invalidation of their claims. He informed them, and informed everyone who claims knowledge, that there is no knowledge beyond it, that even if the water of the sea were ink, and every branch and stick in all the trees of the world were a pen, and they wrote with them, the water of the sea and the branches of the trees would be exhausted, while the words of my Lord, which carry the divine sciences and knowledge, indicate it and guide to it, would not be exhausted. Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah the Mighty; glory be to Allah, to whom the knowledge of everything has come to its end, and He is over all things competent.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is one God."﴾ Allah, exalted is He, commands His Messenger to say to the polytheists who ask him for miracles like those given to Moses and Jesus: "I am only a human being like you; I am not able to do what you are not able to do. The difference between us is that it is revealed to me the matter from my Lord, and it is not revealed to you. It is revealed to me that your God, i.e., your true object of worship and your truthful Lord, is one God: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old." And His saying ﴿So whoever hopes﴾, i.e., aspires and awaits ﴿for the meeting with his Lord﴾, out of fear of Him and desire for Him, ﴿let him do righteous deeds﴾ while being a believer, certain, ﴿and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, for polytheism nullifies and invalidates deeds. By this, his hope is sincere and his expectation is righteous and correct.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.
2. Explanation of the best of gardens, which is the highest Firdaws.
3. The knowledge of Allah is infinite, because His words are infinite.
4. Affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, exalted is He.
5. Affirmation of the humanity of the Prophet ﷺ, and that he is not merely a spirit or a light, as the extremist Batiniyya say.
6. Affirmation of monotheism and condemnation of polytheism.
7. Affirmation that showing off is polytheism, since it is reported that the verse was revealed to explain the ruling on a person who strives while desiring the face of Allah but also wishing to be seen in his place among people, who prays and fasts and loves to be praised for that.
